findings.problem: s0007 泰始初 is an era-opening label, not a closed Gregorian year. Conventional 泰始元年 = AD 265, but the era opened in the twelfth month and 十二月丙寅 is already AD 266. The onOrAfter 265 bound is as far as this chapter can go.
findings.action: Keep unresolved:true with onOrAfter 265. Do not close 265–265 or 266–266 from 初 alone, and do not approve the Taishi office as a supported life year.

findings.problem: s0024 惠帝遣加 is written after the 永興中 victory but is not itself dated 永興. Yongxing opens AD 304; Hui's later death is not in this chapter and cannot close 304–306.
findings.action: Keep unresolved:true with onOrAfter 304. Do not close the honor to the Yongxing span or to an imported death year, and do not approve the row.

units.zh: 家世孝廉，以儒學顯。
units.en: His clan had long supplied xiaolian candidates and was known for Confucian learning.
units.literal: For generations his family had produced men recommended as xiaolian, and they were eminent in Confucian scholarship.

units.zh: 父溫，為太官令。
units.en: His father Zhang Wen held the post of Director of the Imperial Kitchen.
units.literal: His father, Zhang Wen, served as Director of the Imperial Kitchen.

units.zh: 軌少明敏好學，有器望，姿儀典則，與同郡皇甫謐善，隱于宜陽女幾山。
units.en: As a young man he was bright, eager to learn, and carried an air of capacity; his deportment was exemplary. He befriended Huangfu Mi of Anding and withdrew to Mount Nüji in Yiyang.
units.literal: In youth Gui was quick, perceptive, and fond of learning; he had presence and high repute, and his bearing was dignified and correct. He was on good terms with Huangfu Mi of the same commandery and lived in seclusion on Mount Nüji in Yiyang.

units.zh: 泰始初，受叔父錫官五品。
units.en: Early in the Taishi reign he was given fifth-rank office through his uncle Zhang Xi.
units.literal: At the beginning of the Taishi era he received from his uncle Xi an office of the fifth rank.

units.zh: 中書監張華與軌論經義及政事損益，甚器之，謂安定中正為蔽善抑才，乃美為之談，以為二品之精。
units.en: Zhang Hua, the Palace Library director, debated classical doctrine and policy with him and came to esteem him deeply, blaming Anding’s impartial judge for hiding talent and praising Zhang Gui as the outstanding man of the second-grade roster.
units.literal: Director of the Palace Library Zhang Hua discussed with him the meaning of the Classics and the gains and losses of government affairs, thought very highly of him, and said that the commandery impartial judge of Anding was concealing the worthy and suppressing talent; he therefore spoke well of him, deeming him the finest among those rated in the second grade.

units.zh: 衛將軍楊珧辟為掾，除太子舍人，累遷散騎常侍、征西軍司。
units.en: Yang Yao, General of the Guards, took him on as a clerk; he was made a gentleman attendant at the heir’s household and eventually promoted through posts to cavalier attendant-in-ordinary and western-expedition army supervisor.
units.literal: General of the Guards Yang Yao summoned him as a clerk; he was appointed Gentleman Attendant at the Heir Apparent’s Household, then rose in stages to Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and Army Supervisor on the Western Expedition.

units.zh: 軌以時方多難，陰圖據河西，筮之，遇《泰》之《觀》，乃投策喜曰：「霸者兆也。」
units.en: Seeing the realm in turmoil, he quietly set his sights on the Hexi region. When he divined with the Changes and drew Tai turning into Guan, he cast the stalks aside and exclaimed, "This is an omen for a hegemon."
units.literal: Because the times were full of troubles, he secretly planned to occupy the region west of the Yellow River. He cast the milfoil and obtained Hexagram Tai changing to Guan; he threw down the stalks and said in joy, "This is an omen for a hegemon."

units.zh: 永甯初，出為護羌校尉、涼州刺史。
units.en: In the first years of Yongning he left the capital as Colonel Who Protects the Qiang and as inspector of Liangzhou.
units.literal: At the beginning of the Yongning era he went out as Colonel Who Protects the Qiang and Inspector of Liangzhou.

units.zh: 于時鮮卑反叛，寇盜從橫，軌到官，即討破之，斬首萬餘級，遂威著西州，化行河右。
units.en: The Xianbei had risen in revolt and raiders swarmed the region; on taking office he struck them down at once, taking over ten thousand heads, until his name carried weight across the west and his rule extended west of the river.
units.literal: At that time the Xianbei rebelled, and bandits ran rampant in every direction. As soon as he reached his post he attacked and defeated them, beheading more than ten thousand, so that his awe spread through the western provinces and his transforming influence reached the right bank of the Yellow River.

units.zh: 以宋配、陰充、氾瑗、陰澹為股肱謀主，征九郡胄子五百人，立學校，始置崇文祭酒，位視別駕，春秋行鄉射之禮。
units.en: Song Pei, Yin Chong, Fan Yuan, and Yin Dan became his principal advisers; he drafted five hundred young nobles from nine commanderies, set up schools, created the post of Libationer for Exalting Culture on a par with chief clerk, and observed the archery rites in spring and autumn.
units.literal: He took Song Pei, Yin Chong, Fan Yuan, and Yin Dan as his chief arms and strategists, conscripted five hundred sons of gentry from the nine commanderies, established schools, and for the first time appointed a Libationer for Exalting Culture, with rank equal to a chief clerk; in spring and autumn he held the village archery ceremony.

units.zh: 秘書監繆世征、少府摯虞夜觀星象，相與言曰：「天下方亂，避難之國唯涼土耳。
units.en: Palace librarian Miao Shizheng and chamberlain Zhi Yu, studying the stars at night, said to each other, "The realm is about to fall into chaos; the only land to flee to is Liangzhou.
units.literal: The Palace Library Supervisor Miao Shizheng and the Chamberlain for the Palace Revenues Zhi Yu watched the stars by night and said to each other, "The realm is about to fall into chaos; the only land to flee to is Liangzhou.

units.zh: 張涼州德量不恆，殆其人乎！」
units.en: They said, "Inspector Zhang’s moral stature was anything but common—perhaps he is the man!"
units.literal: Inspector Zhang’s virtue and capacity are not ordinary—perhaps he is the man!"

units.zh: 及河間、成都二王之難，遣兵三千，東赴京師。
units.en: When civil war erupted between the princes of Hejian and Chengdu, he dispatched three thousand soldiers toward Luoyang.
units.literal: When the troubles of the Princes of Hejian and Chengdu broke out, he sent three thousand troops east to the capital.

units.zh: 初，漢末金城人陽成遠殺太守以叛，郡人馮忠赴屍號哭，嘔血而死。
units.en: Earlier, in late Han, Yangcheng Yuan of Jincheng had murdered the grand administrator and risen in revolt; Feng Zhong of the same commandery threw himself on the body and wept until he coughed blood and died.
units.literal: In the beginning, at the end of the Han, a man of Jincheng commandery named Yang Cheng Yuan killed the grand administrator and rebelled; a man of the commandery, Feng Zhong, went to the corpse and wailed until he vomited blood and died.

units.zh: 參、賢慚悔，自相和釋。
units.en: Pang Can and Ma Xian, stricken with remorse, made peace between themselves.
units.literal: Can and Xian were ashamed and regretful and reconciled with each other.

units.zh: 軌皆祭其墓而旌其子孫。
units.en: Zhang Gui offered sacrifices at their graves and ennobled their posterity.
units.literal: Gui sacrificed at all their tombs and honored their descendants.

units.zh: 永興中，鮮卑若羅拔能皆為寇，軌遣司馬宋配擊之，斬拔能，俘十餘萬口，威名大震。
units.en: During Yongxing, when Xianbei leader Ruoluo Baneng pillaged the frontier, he sent Major Song Pei, who slew Baneng and took over a hundred thousand captives, so that his fame resounded far and wide.
units.literal: In the Yongxing era the Xianbei Raluo and Baneng both raided as bandits; Gui sent his Major Song Pei against them. Song Pei beheaded Baneng and captured more than a hundred thousand persons, and Gui’s renown shook the realm.

units.zh: 惠帝遣加安西將軍，封安樂鄉侯，邑千戶。
units.en: Emperor Hui added him as General Who Pacifies the West, enfeoffed him as marquis of Anle township with a thousand-household fief.
units.literal: The Emperor Hui sent orders promoting him to General Who Guards the West and enfeoffing him as Marquis of Anle Township with a fief of one thousand households.

units.zh: 於是大城姑臧。
units.en: He then undertook a major expansion of Guzang.
units.literal: Thereupon he greatly enlarged the city of Guzang.

units.zh: 其城本匈奴所築也，南北七里，東西三里，地有龍形，故名臥龍城。
units.en: The walls had been raised by the Xiongnu—seven li north–south, three li east–west—with ground shaped like a crouching dragon, hence the name “Recumbent Dragon.”
units.literal: The city had originally been built by the Xiongnu: seven li from north to south and three li from east to west; the terrain resembled a dragon, so it was called the Recumbent Dragon City.

units.zh: 初，漢末博士敦煌侯瑾謂其門人曰：「後城西泉水當竭，有雙闕起其上，與東門相望。
units.en: Long before, the Han scholar Hou Jin of Dunhuang told his students, "Later the western spring would one day fail and twin towers would stand there, aligned with the east gate.
units.literal: In the beginning, at the end of the Han, the erudite Hou Jin of Dunhuang said to his disciples, "Later the spring west of the city will dry up, and a pair of gate-towers will rise upon it, facing the east gate.

units.zh: 今宜悉徙，以絕後患。」
units.en: Move every one of them now and leave no future threat.”
units.literal: Now it is fitting to move them all and thereby cut off later trouble.’

units.zh: 寔不納。
units.en: Zhang Shi did not follow the advice.
units.literal: Shi did not accept this.

units.zh: 儒黨果叛，寔進平之。
units.en: Qu’s clique rose anyway, and Zhang Shi marched again to crush them.
units.literal: The Qu faction indeed rebelled; Shi advanced and pacified them.

units.zh: 湣帝即位，進位司空，固讓。
units.en: Emperor Min promoted him to minister of works, which he refused.
units.literal: When Emperor Min ascended the throne, Gui’s rank was advanced to Minister of Works; he firmly declined.

units.zh: 太府參軍索輔言於軌曰：「古以金貝皮幣為貨，息穀帛量度之秏。
units.en: Suo Fu of the grand treasury told him: “Antiquity used metal, shell, and cloth as money to avoid the waste of weighing grain and silk.
units.literal: Adjutant of the grand treasury Suo Fu said to Gui, ‘In antiquity shell, cowrie, hide, and cloth served as currency, sparing the waste of measuring grain and silk.

units.zh: 二漢制五銖錢，通易不滯。
units.en: Han’s five-zhu cash kept trade moving smoothly.
units.literal: The two Han dynasties minted the five-zhu coin, so exchange flowed without obstruction.

units.zh: 泰始中，河西荒廢，遂不用錢。
units.en: During Taishi the Hexi region was so ruined that money disappeared.
units.literal: In the Taishi era the west of the river was desolate and coins fell out of use.

units.zh: 裂匹以為段數。
units.en: Silk was torn into arbitrary lengths for barter.
units.literal: They tore bolts of silk into counted segments.

units.zh: 縑布既壞，市易又難，徒壞女工，不任衣用，弊之甚也。
units.en: Damaged silk ruined commerce, wasted women’s labor, and still could not clothe anyone—a thorough evil.
units.literal: Once fine cloth was ruined, market trade became difficult, vainly harming women’s weaving yet unfit for clothing—harm indeed was extreme.

units.zh: 今中州雖亂，此方主安全，宜復五銖以濟通變之會。」
units.en: The heartland is at war, yet we are safe; restoring the five-zhu will ease exchange.”
units.literal: Now the central plain is in turmoil, but this region is secure; it is fitting to restore the five-zhu coin to meet the needs of circulation.’

units.zh: 軌納之，立制准布用錢，錢遂大行，人賴其利。
units.en: Zhang Gui agreed, set a cloth-to-coin standard, and currency flourished to the people’s gain.
units.literal: Gui accepted this, established regulations pegging cloth to coin, and coinage then circulated widely; people relied on its benefit.

units.zh: 是時劉曜寇北地，軌又遣參軍麹陶領三千人衛長安。
units.en: When Liu Yao struck Beidi, he sent Qu Tao with three thousand to reinforce Chang’an.
units.literal: At that time Liu Yao raided Beidi; Gui again sent adjutant Qu Tao with three thousand men to defend Chang’an.

units.zh: 帝遣大鴻臚辛攀拜軌侍中、太尉、涼州牧、西平公，軌又固辭。
units.en: The court dispatched Xin Pan to name him attendant-in-chief, grand commandant, Liangzhou governor, and duke of Xiping—all declined again.
units.literal: The emperor sent Grand Herald Xin Pan to appoint Gui as palace attendant, grand commandant, governor of Liangzhou, and Duke of Xiping; again Gui firmly declined.

units.zh: 在州十三年，寢疾，遺令曰：「吾無德於人，今疾病彌留，殆將命也。
units.en: After thirteen years in office, mortally ill, he dictated: “I have done little good for anyone; my sickness lingers and the end is near.
units.literal: Thirteen years in the province, lying ill, he left instructions saying, ‘I have lacked virtue toward others; now my illness lingers and death is near.

units.zh: 文武將佐咸當弘盡忠規，務安百姓，上思報國，下以寧家。
units.en: Let every officer strive for loyal counsel, comfort the people, serve the throne above, and settle their homes below.
units.literal: All civil and military assistants ought to enlarge loyal counsel, work to secure the common people, think above of repaying the state, and below of quieting their households.

units.zh: 素棺薄葬，無藏金玉。
units.en: Bury me in a plain coffin without gold or jade.
units.literal: Use plain coffins and spare burial; do not bury gold or jade.

references.title: 永宁 (西晋)
references.quote: 永宁（ 301年四月—302年十一月）是西晋皇帝晋惠帝司马衷的第五个年号
references.reason: Confirms conventional 永寧元年 = AD 301 and that the era opened in the fourth month, so 永甯初 as a closed 301 reign-year label does not cross a Western New Year.

references.title: 永兴 (西晋)
references.quote: 永兴（ 304年十二月—306年六月）是西晋皇帝晋惠帝司马衷的第八个年号
references.reason: Confirms conventional 永興 = AD 304–306 as the era span used for 永興中. Conventional year labels need not equal the Gregorian year of the twelfth-month opening.

references.title: 永嘉 (西晋)
references.quote: 永嘉（ 307年—313年四月）是西晋皇帝晋怀帝司馬熾的年号
references.reason: Confirms conventional 永嘉元年 = AD 307 (opened in the first month) for 永嘉初 closures.

references.title: 建兴 (西晋)
references.quote: 建兴（ 313年四月—317年三月）是西晋皇帝晉愍帝司馬鄴的年号
references.reason: Confirms 建興元年 = AD 313 and that Jianxing 4 is the conventional fourth year (AD 316) used from 四載於茲, not from a written 建興四年 in the chapter.

references.title: 建兴 (西晋)
references.quote: 建兴四年晉愍帝投降前赵，西晋灭亡。
references.reason: Independent witness that Chang'an's surrender belongs to Jianxing 4 / AD 316, matching 四載於茲 after a 313 accession.

references.title: 大兴 (东晋)
references.quote: 大兴（或作太兴； 318年三月—321年）是东晋皇帝晉元帝司馬睿的第二个年号
references.reason: Confirms 太興元年 = AD 318 and therefore 建興六年 in the same year, used only as context for later Zhang Shi / Yuan Di rows.

references.title: 泰始 (西晋)
references.quote: 晉武帝改元泰始时（乙酉年十二月丙寅）已是公元266年2月8日。
references.reason: Shows why 泰始初 cannot be closed as Gregorian 265: the era-opening day is already AD 266. Supports leaving claim-566 unresolved with onOrAfter 265.

references.title: 通鉴纪事本末卷十三下
references.quote: 己丑，轨薨，长史张玺等表世子寔摄父位。
references.reason: The Tongjian tradition dates Zhang Gui's death to Jianxing 2 / the fifth month, which is the conventional 314 reading. The chapter never writes 二年, so that witness stays competing with inclusive 在州十三年 / 313 rather than winning.

references.title: 建兴 (西晋)
references.quote: 建兴（ 313年四月—317年三月）是西晋皇帝晉愍帝司馬鄴的年号
references.reason: Primary calendar witness for Min’s Jianxing: year 1 = AD 313, year 2 = 314, year 4 = 316; Former Liang 建興六年 = 318.

references.title: 东晋年号查询 — 国学迷
references.quote: 东晋[咸和]八年 前凉[建兴]二十一年
references.reason: Corroborates 咸和八年 = AD 333 and that Former Liang 建興二十一年 is the same conventional year as s0467 猶稱建興二十一年, without converting Jun’s private calendar into a second Western endpoint.

references.title: 建兴 (西晋)
references.quote: 建興四十二年（354年）正月，張祚改元為和平元年。
references.reason: Confirms Former Liang continued 建興 so year 42 = Heping 1 = AD 354, matching Jinshu s0842/s0655 juxtaposition. Also lists 四十三 = 355 and 四十九 = 361.

question: What chronology is actually known? Genuine one-sided knowledge is allowed; missing exact years alone need not invalidate a supported bound. Preserve true conversion/owner/period conflicts and do not invent exact years or unsupported endpoints.
